title: Empagliflozin and Progression of Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: SGLT2 inhibitors confer renal and cardiovascular protection in patients with diabetes. Methods: In this double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 6,609 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease were assigned to receive empagliflozin 10 mg daily or matching placebo. The primary outcome was progression of kidney disease or cardiovascular death. Results: Over a median follow-up of 2.0 years, progression of kidney disease or death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 432 of 3,304 patients (13.1%) in the empagliflozin group and in 558 of 3,305 patients (16.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.64 to 0.82; p < 0.001). Serious adverse events were balanced between arms. Conclusions: Among patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, empagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of kidney disease progression and cardiovascular death compared with placebo.

title: Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes with Semaglutide in Type 2 Diabetes: Extended Follow-up of the SUSTAIN-6 Randomized Trial
abstract: Objective: To assess the prolonged efficacy and cardiovascular safety of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus at high cardiovascular risk. Research Design and Methods: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 3,297 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease receiving subcutaneous semaglutide (0.5 mg or 1.0 mg weekly) or placebo. The primary composite outcome was cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (3-point MACE). Results: After 24 months, the primary outcome occurred in 108 of 1,648 patients (6.6%) on semaglutide versus 146 of 1,649 patients (8.9%) on placebo (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.95; p = 0.02). New or worsening nephropathy was also significantly reduced in the semaglutide group (hazard ratio, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.46 to 0.88). Conclusions: Once-weekly semaglutide significantly reduced major adverse cardiovascular events and diabetic nephropathy in high-risk patients with type 2 diabetes.

title: Comparative Cardiovascular and Renal Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and CKD: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
abstract: Background: Both SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve cardiorenal outcomes in type 2 diabetes, but direct head-to-head trials remain scarce. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of 28 randomized controlled trials involving 167,420 participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease. Results: SGLT2 inhibitors were superior to GLP-1 RAs in reducing hospitalization for heart failure (relative risk [RR] 0.68 vs 0.90; p for difference = 0.003) and end-stage kidney disease progression (RR 0.61 vs 0.82; p for difference = 0.012). Conversely, GLP-1 RAs conferred a greater reduction in nonfatal stroke compared with SGLT2 inhibitors (RR 0.85 vs 0.99; p for difference = 0.041). Both drug classes demonstrated equivalent efficacy in reducing 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (RR 0.88 vs 0.87; p = 0.76). Conclusions: In patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors provide greater protection against heart failure hospitalization and renal progression, whereas GLP-1 RAs offer superior stroke prevention.

title: Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease and Concomitant Heart Failure: Secondary Analysis of DAPA-CKD
abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease frequently coexists with heart failure, compounding mortality risk. Methods: We analyzed participants in the randomized, double-blind DAPA-CKD trial who had baseline chronic kidney disease and heart failure. Patients received dapagliflozin 10 mg or placebo once daily. Results: Among 4,304 participants, 674 (15.7%) had heart failure at baseline. Dapagliflozin reduced the primary composite outcome of sustained estimated GFR decline of >=50%, end-stage kidney disease, or renal/CV death (HR 0.58; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.74) consistently across patients with and without heart failure (interaction p = 0.62). All-cause mortality was significantly attenuated (HR 0.69; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.88). Conclusions: Dapagliflozin consistently prevents renal progression and cardiovascular death in patients with chronic kidney disease regardless of baseline heart failure status.

title: Combined Therapy with SGLT2 Inhibitors and GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Resistant Type 2 Diabetes: A Real-World Observational Cohort Study
abstract: Objective: To investigate the real-world glycaemic and cardiorenal impact of combination therapy using SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists. Methods: A retrospective cohort study observed 12,450 adult patients with refractory type 2 diabetes mellitus receiving either combination therapy (SGLT2i + GLP-1 RA) or intensified insulin regimen between 2019 and 2023. Results: At 36 months, the dual combination cohort achieved greater mean HbA1c reduction (-1.42% vs -0.85%; p < 0.001) and sustained weight loss (-4.8 kg vs +2.1 kg; p < 0.001). Major adverse cardiovascular events were reduced by 22% (adjusted HR 0.78; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.91). No synergistic increase in ketoacidosis or pancreatitis was observed. Conclusions: Combination SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA therapy delivers superior cardiometabolic outcomes and durable glycemic control compared to intensified insulin in resistant type 2 diabetes.

title: Sotorasib versus Docetaxel for Previously Treated Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer with KRAS G12C Mutation: The CodeBreaK 200 Phase 3 Randomized Trial
abstract: Background: Sotorasib was the first approved KRAS G12C inhibitor for advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: In the global, open-label, Phase 3 CodeBreaK 200 trial, 345 patients with advanced KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC previously treated with platinum doublet and checkpoint inhibitor were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral sotorasib 960 mg daily or intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. Results: Sotorasib significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) compared with docetaxel (median PFS 5.6 months vs 4.5 months; hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.86; p = 0.002). The objective response rate was 28.1% with sotorasib versus 13.2% with docetaxel. Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events were less frequent with sotorasib (33.1% vs 40.4%). Overall survival did not differ significantly between arms (median 10.6 vs 11.3 months; HR 1.01). Conclusions: Sotorasib demonstrated significant progression-free survival benefit and a more favorable safety profile compared with docetaxel in previously treated KRAS G12C advanced NSCLC.

title: Acquired Resistance Mechanisms to Sotorasib in KRAS G12C Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Secondary Mutations and Bypass Receptor Activation
abstract: Background: Despite initial tumor regression, acquired resistance to sotorasib universally develops in KRAS G12C mutated NSCLC. Methods: We performed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and paired pre- and post-progression tumor tissue next-generation sequencing in 43 patients with advanced KRAS G12C NSCLC who progressed on sotorasib. Results: Acquired secondary KRAS mutations affecting the drug-binding pocket or switch II region (including Y96D, A59S, G13D, and Q61H) were detected in 18 patients (41.9%). Bypass signaling mechanisms were identified in 15 patients (34.9%), predominantly MET gene amplification (14.0%), ERBB2 amplifications (9.3%), and oncogenic fusions in RET and ALK. In vitro functional models confirmed that MET amplification drives resistance via sustained ERK and AKT phosphorylation, which was successfully reversed by co-treatment with sotorasib and the MET inhibitor capmatinib. Conclusions: Resistance to sotorasib is heterogeneous, driven by secondary KRAS mutations and bypass activation of receptor tyrosine kinases such as MET; combination therapeutic strategies are required.

title: Intracranial Activity and Systemic Efficacy of Adagrasib in KRAS G12C-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer with Active Brain Metastases
abstract: Background: Central nervous system (CNS) metastases are frequent and carry poor prognosis in KRAS G12C mutated NSCLC. Methods: In the KRYSTAL-1 Phase 1b/2 study cohort, patients with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced NSCLC and untreated, active CNS metastases received adagrasib 600 mg orally twice daily. Results: Among 25 evaluable patients with baseline active brain metastases, intracranial objective response rate was 42.0% (95% CI, 20.3 to 66.5), with a median intracranial duration of response of 12.7 months. Systemic objective response rate was 36.0%. Median progression-free survival was 5.4 months. Cerebrospinal fluid pharmacokinetic analysis demonstrated adagrasib concentrations exceeding the biochemical IC50. Conclusions: Adagrasib exhibits clinically meaningful intracranial activity and durable CNS disease control in patients with KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC and active brain metastases.

title: MET Amplification as a Common Bypass Resistance Mechanism to Covalent KRAS G12C Inhibitors in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: Background: Targeted covalent inhibition of KRAS G12C has reshaped NSCLC therapy, yet bypass track activation compromises durability. Methods: We analyzed genomic profiling from 68 patients with advanced NSCLC exhibiting disease progression following therapy with sotorasib or adagrasib. Results: High-level MET gene amplification was detected in 13.2% of post-treatment biopsies. Functional validation in patient-derived organoids confirmed that MET hyperactivation restores downstream MAPK and PI3K/mTOR signaling despite complete covalent KRAS G12C inactivation. Pharmacological inhibition with crizotinib or capmatinib restored sensitivity to KRAS G12C blockade both in vitro and in murine xenografts. Conclusions: MET amplification is a validated recurrent bypass mechanism of resistance to KRAS G12C inhibitors in NSCLC, supporting dual-inhibition clinical trials.

title: Combined SHP2 and KRAS G12C Inhibition Suppresses Adaptive Feedback Resistance in Lung Adenocarcinoma Models
abstract: Background: Rapid reactivation of wild-type RAS and RTK signaling limits single-agent KRAS G12C inhibitor efficacy. Methods: We evaluated the synergistic antitumor activity of combining the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor TNO155 with sotorasib in KRAS G12C mutant lung adenocarcinoma cell lines and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Results: Single-agent sotorasib induced rapid rebound ERK phosphorylation within 24 hours. Addition of TNO155 blocked SOS1-mediated nucleotide exchange, preventing adaptive RAS pathway reactivation. In vivo PDX models demonstrated prolonged tumor regression with dual inhibition (mean tumor reduction -78% vs -32% with monotherapy; p < 0.001) without dose-limiting toxicity. Conclusions: Combining SHP2 inhibition with covalent KRAS G12C blockade prevents adaptive feedback resistance and deepens therapeutic responses in preclinical NSCLC models.

title: Safety, Immunogenicity, and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Vaccine in Children Aged 6 Months to 4 Years: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Young children require safe and protective vaccination against SARS-CoV-2. Methods: In this Phase 2/3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 4,526 children aged 6 months through 4 years received three 3-ug doses of the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine or placebo. Immunogenicity was evaluated by neutralizing antibody titers, and vaccine efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19 was assessed. Results: In children 6 to 23 months and 2 to 4 years of age, neutralizing geometric mean ratios met prespecified immunobridging noninferiority criteria compared with young adults. Observed vaccine efficacy against symptomatic illness was 73.2% (95% CI, 43.8 to 87.6). Reactogenicity was mild to moderate and transient; incidence of fever was low (7.2%), and no cases of myocarditis, pericarditis, or anaphylaxis were reported during the follow-up window. Conclusions: A three-dose primary series of 3-ug BNT162b2 was safe, immunogenic, and efficacious against COVID-19 in children aged 6 months to 4 years.

title: Evaluation of mRNA-1273 COVID-19 Vaccine in Infants and Young Children: A Randomized Controlled Phase 2-3 Trial
abstract: Background: Vaccination strategies for pediatric populations require rigorous randomized assessment. Methods: We conducted a randomized, observer-blinded, placebo-controlled trial of the mRNA-1273 vaccine (two 25-ug doses) in 6,711 children aged 6 months through 5 years. Results: The primary immunogenicity objective was met, with neutralizing antibody titers noninferior to those in young adults (ratio 1.28; 95% CI, 1.12 to 1.47). Vaccine efficacy against confirmed infection was 50.6% (95% CI, 21.4 to 68.6) in children 6 to 23 months and 36.8% (95% CI, 12.5 to 54.0) in children 2 to 5 years during predominant Omicron transmission. Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2 with no vaccine-associated serious adverse events or myocarditis observed. Conclusions: Two 25-ug doses of mRNA-1273 were safe and generated robust humoral immune responses in infants and young children.

title: Surveillance of Myopericarditis Following mRNA Vaccination in Adolescents and Children: A Population-Based Multicenter Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Concerns regarding myopericarditis after mRNA vaccination require quantified surveillance in pediatric populations. Methods: We conducted a population-based multicenter cohort study analyzing electronic health records of 1,240,000 vaccinated individuals aged 5 to 17 years who received mRNA vaccines between 2021 and 2023. Results: Across 2.1 million doses administered, 38 confirmed cases of myopericarditis were identified, corresponding to an overall incidence of 1.8 cases per 100,000 doses. Incidence was highest in adolescent males aged 12 to 17 years following dose 2 (6.2 per 100,000 doses), whereas incidence in children aged 5 to 11 years was extremely low (0.3 per 100,000 doses). Clinical course was mild in 92% of cases, with rapid symptom resolution within 72 hours and normal echocardiographic recovery at 6-month follow-up. Conclusions: Myopericarditis following mRNA vaccination is rare in pediatric populations, substantially rarer in children under 12, and clinically benign in the majority of patients.

title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Bivalent mRNA Booster Vaccines in Immunocompromised Pediatric Patients
abstract: Background: Immunocompromised children have heightened vulnerability to severe viral respiratory illness. Methods: In a multicenter randomized controlled trial, 412 pediatric patients aged 5 to 17 years with solid organ transplants or primary immunodeficiencies received either a bivalent mRNA booster or monotherapy standard-of-care booster. Results: At day 28 post-vaccination, bivalent booster recipients achieved 4.3-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against evolving variants compared with control (p < 0.001). Cellular T-cell responses were preserved in 82% of immunosuppressed patients. Transient local injection-site soreness was the most frequent reaction; no allograft rejection episodes occurred. Conclusions: Bivalent mRNA booster vaccination is well-tolerated and significantly enhances humoral and cellular protection in immunocompromised children.

title: A Phase 3 Randomized Controlled Trial of an Investigational Pediatric mRNA Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine in Infants
abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a primary cause of hospitalization in young infants. Methods: We conducted a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluating an investigational lipid nanoparticle-formulated mRNA vaccine encoding prefusion RSV F protein in 3,850 healthy infants aged 2 to 12 months. Results: Over the RSV season, vaccine efficacy against medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease was 81.4% (95% CI, 66.8 to 89.6; p < 0.001). Severe RSV illness was reduced by 87.5%. Adverse event profiles were comparable between vaccine and placebo cohorts, with no signal of vaccine-enhanced respiratory disease. Conclusions: The investigational pediatric mRNA RSV vaccine conferred high efficacy against lower respiratory tract disease and showed favorable safety in infants.

title: Renal Denervation versus Sham Procedure in Patients with Resistant Hypertension: Long-Term Follow-up of the SPYRAL HTN-ON MED Randomized Trial
abstract: Background: Catheter-based renal denervation has emerged as a potential intervention for drug-resistant hypertension. Methods: In this randomized, sham-controlled trial, 337 patients with resistant hypertension confirmed by ambulatory blood pressure monitoring while adhering to stable antihypertensive regimens were assigned to radiofrequency renal denervation or sham procedure. Results: At 36 months, the renal denervation group achieved a significant reduction in 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure compared with the sham group (treatment difference -4.8 mm Hg; 95% CI, -8.1 to -1.5; p = 0.005). Antihypertensive medication burden remained lower in the denervation arm. No renal artery stenosis or procedural vascular complications were reported during extended follow-up. Conclusions: Catheter-based renal denervation produces safe, durable reductions in ambulatory blood pressure in patients with uncontrolled resistant hypertension receiving concurrent medical therapy.

title: Dual Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System Blockade versus Monotherapy in Diabetic Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
abstract: Background: Combining ACE inhibitors with angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) has been investigated for blood pressure and renal endpoints in diabetic hypertension. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 randomized clinical trials comprising 19,850 participants with diabetes and hypertension comparing dual RAAS inhibition with monotherapy. Results: Dual RAAS blockade produced modest additional systolic blood pressure reduction (-2.4 mm Hg; 95% CI, -3.8 to -1.0; p = 0.001) and albuminuria reduction, but doubled the risk of hyperkalemia (relative risk 2.14; 95% CI, 1.76 to 2.60; p < 0.001) and acute kidney injury (RR 1.62; 95% CI, 1.28 to 2.05). All-cause mortality was unchanged (RR 1.02; p = 0.74). Conclusions: Dual RAAS blockade increases adverse renal events and hyperkalemia without improving survival, and cannot be recommended for routine management of diabetic hypertension.

title: Phase 2 Trial of Baxdrostat, an Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitor, for Treatment-Resistant Hypertension
abstract: Background: Excessive aldosterone synthesis contributes to resistant hypertension, but selective inhibition has historically been pharmacologically challenging. Methods: In this Phase 2, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 275 patients with treatment-resistant hypertension taking at least three antihypertensive agents received baxdrostat (0.5 mg, 1 mg, or 2 mg once daily) or placebo for 12 weeks. Results: Dose-dependent reductions in seated systolic blood pressure were observed. Baxdrostat 2 mg daily reduced seated systolic BP by 20.3 mm Hg compared with a 9.3 mm Hg reduction in the placebo group (placebo-adjusted difference -11.0 mm Hg; 95% CI, -16.4 to -5.5; p < 0.001). No cases of adrenocortical insufficiency occurred, and hyperkalemia was infrequent (3.2%). Conclusions: Highly selective aldosterone synthase inhibition with baxdrostat leads to substantial blood pressure reduction in patients with treatment-resistant hypertension.

title: Visit-to-Visit Blood Pressure Variability and Incidence of Cognitive Impairment in Hypertensive Older Adults: A 10-Year Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Blood pressure variability has been implicated in target-organ microvascular damage and dementia. Methods: A prospective observational cohort followed 4,890 hypertensive patients aged 65 years and older over 10 years. Visit-to-visit blood pressure variability was quantified using coefficient of variation (CV) of systolic blood pressure across annual clinic visits. Cognitive impairment was evaluated using adjudicated DSM criteria and MoCA scores. Results: Patients in the highest quintile of systolic BP variability had an increased risk of cognitive decline and vascular dementia compared with the lowest quintile (adjusted HR 1.54; 95% CI, 1.28 to 1.86; p < 0.001). The association remained robust after adjusting for mean absolute blood pressure. Conclusions: Greater visit-to-visit blood pressure variability independently predicts long-term cognitive decline and vascular dementia in elderly hypertensive patients.

title: Intensive Dietary Sodium Restriction and Aerobic Exercise versus Antihypertensive Monotherapy in Stage 1 Hypertension: A Randomized Trial
abstract: Background: Comparative efficacy of lifestyle modifications versus first-line pharmacotherapy in early hypertension remains debated. Methods: In an open-label randomized trial, 520 young adults (aged 25-45 years) with newly diagnosed stage 1 hypertension were randomized to intensive lifestyle modification (sodium intake < 1500 mg/day plus 150 min/week structured aerobic exercise) or amlodipine 5 mg monotherapy for 24 weeks. Results: Both interventions resulted in significant systolic blood pressure reductions (-11.2 mm Hg in lifestyle vs -12.4 mm Hg in amlodipine; difference -1.2 mm Hg; 95% CI, -3.1 to 0.7; p = 0.22, demonstrating noninferiority). Lifestyle intervention yielded significant improvements in body mass index and insulin sensitivity. Conclusions: Intensive lifestyle intervention is noninferior to amlodipine monotherapy in reducing blood pressure among young adults with uncomplicated stage 1 hypertension.

title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease: Final Clinical and Biomarker Analysis of the Clarity AD Phase 3 Trial
abstract: Background: Lecanemab, an IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting soluble amyloid-beta protofibrils, was evaluated in early Alzheimer's disease. Methods: In this 18-month, multicenter, double-blind Phase 3 trial, 1,795 patients with early Alzheimer's disease (mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia with confirmed amyloid pathology) were randomized to intravenous lecanemab (10 mg/kg biweekly) or placebo. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) at 18 months. Results: Lecanemab reduced mean CDR-SB decline by 27% compared with placebo (mean change 1.21 vs 1.66; difference -0.45; 95% CI, -0.67 to -0.23; p < 0.001). Amyloid PET burden was substantially reduced. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema (ARIA-E) occurred in 12.6% of lecanemab recipients compared with 1.7% in placebo. Conclusions: In early Alzheimer's disease, lecanemab significantly reduced markers of amyloid pathology and produced moderately less clinical decline on cognitive and functional measures, accompanied by adverse events including ARIA.

title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: Importance: Donanemab targets brain amyloid plaque clearance and alters disease progression in early Alzheimer disease. Objective: To evaluate safety and efficacy of donanemab in early symptomatic Alzheimer disease. Design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial enrolling 1,736 participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer disease stratified by baseline tau PET levels. Participants received donanemab (700 mg for first 3 doses, then 1400 mg every 4 weeks) or placebo for 76 weeks. Results: In the low/medium-tau population, donanemab significantly slowed clinical progression on the integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) by 35.1% (p < 0.001) and on CDR-SB by 36.0% (p < 0.001). At 76 weeks, 80.1% of donanemab-treated participants achieved amyloid clearance. ARIA-E occurred in 24.0% of participants on donanemab versus 2.1% on placebo. Conclusions: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical progression in early symptomatic Alzheimer disease, with substantial amyloid clearance and recognizable ARIA risk.

title: Spatiotemporal Kinetics of Tau Aggregation Measured by 18F-MK-6240 PET and Longitudinal Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Background: Neurofibrillary tau tangle accumulation closely tracks clinical symptom severity and neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease. Methods: A prospective cohort of 280 individuals across the Alzheimer's continuum underwent longitudinal 18F-MK-6240 tau PET imaging and neuropsychological testing over 4 years. Results: Entorhinal tau burden predicted subsequent neocortical tau propagation and accelerated MMSE score decline (beta = -0.42; p < 0.001). Patients presenting with advanced Braak stage V-VI neocortical tau aggregation displayed relentless cognitive deterioration refractory to standard anti-amyloid baseline levels. Conclusions: Neocortical tau deposition represents a distinct and aggressive phase of Alzheimer's pathophysiology that requires direct tau-targeting modalities.

title: Microglial Phenotypes and Complement Activation Drive Synaptic Pruning in Late-Stage Alzheimer's Disease Neuropathology
abstract: Background: Chronic neuroinflammation in advanced Alzheimer's disease promotes synapse loss and accelerates disease severity. Methods: We examined post-mortem brain specimens from 85 patients with severe, late-stage Alzheimer's disease (Braak stage V/VI) using single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. Results: Disease-associated microglia (DAM) exhibited pronounced upregulation of complement cascade components (C1q, C3) and phagocytic receptors, mediating aberrant engulfment of synaptic terminals. Genetic ablation of C3 in transgenic tauopathy mouse models attenuated synaptic loss without altering total phosphorylated tau burden. Conclusions: Synaptic destruction in late-stage Alzheimer's disease is driven by complement-mediated microglial engulfment, identifying complement inhibition as a candidate target for advanced stages.

title: Investigating Non-Pharmacological Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy in Rodent Models of Neurodegeneration: Total Inability to Clear Advanced Tau Tangles
abstract: Background: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) has been promoted colloquially for brain health, but scientific evidence regarding pathological protein clearance remains sparse. Methods: Aged transgenic P301S tauopathy mice with established advanced Stage IV-equivalent neurofibrillary pathology were randomized to receive 40 sessions of HBOT (2.0 atmospheres absolute with 100% oxygen for 60 min daily) or normobaric room air. Post-treatment brain tissue was assessed for insoluble hyperphosphorylated tau aggregates, amyloid levels, and stereological neuronal survival. Results: HBOT failed to reduce insoluble hyperphosphorylated tau levels in cortex or hippocampus compared with control (tau pS396/total tau ratio 1.04 vs 0.99; p = 0.78). Neocortical neurofibrillary tangle burden was unchanged, and advanced neuronal loss was not prevented. No clinical or histological reversal of advanced tau pathology was observed. Conclusions: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy produces no clearance or reversal of advanced tau tangle pathology in established neurodegenerative models, underscoring the lack of biological rationale for HBOT in advanced stage tauopathies.

title: Metformin Monotherapy and Long-Term Reduction in Myocardial Infarction and All-Cause Mortality in Type 2 Diabetes: 10-Year Follow-up of UKPDS
abstract: Objective: To assess the prolonged legacy effect of intensive blood-glucose control with metformin on macrovascular complications in overweight patients with type 2 diabetes. Methods: Post-trial monitoring cohort of the UK Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) followed 1,704 newly diagnosed overweight patients assigned to intensive therapy with metformin or conventional dietary therapy. Results: In the metformin group, significant risk reductions persisted during 10 years of post-trial follow-up for any diabetes-related endpoint (risk reduction 21%; p = 0.01), myocardial infarction (risk reduction 33%; hazard ratio 0.67; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.89; p = 0.005), and all-cause mortality (risk reduction 27%; hazard ratio 0.73; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.92; p = 0.008), despite an early loss of glycaemic differences between groups. Conclusions: Intensive blood-glucose control with metformin confers a durable legacy effect, significantly reducing long-term myocardial infarction risk and mortality in type 2 diabetes.

title: Comparative Cardiovascular Safety of Metformin versus Sulfonylureas in Older Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Population Study
abstract: Background: First-line antidiabetic selection in older patients must balance efficacy and cardiovascular safety. Methods: In a retrospective cohort of 34,200 veterans aged 65 years and older initiating monotherapy with metformin or sulfonylureas, participants were followed for composite major adverse cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death). Results: Initiation of metformin monotherapy was associated with a 20% lower hazard of composite cardiovascular events compared with sulfonylurea monotherapy (adjusted HR 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.90; p < 0.001), driven primarily by lower incidence of fatal and nonfatal myocardial infarction. Hypoglycemia rates were substantially lower with metformin (1.4% vs 6.8%). Conclusions: Metformin is associated with superior cardiovascular safety and lower myocardial infarction risk compared to sulfonylureas in older patients with type 2 diabetes.

title: Tezepelumab in Adults and Adolescents with Severe, Uncontrolled Asthma: The NAVIGATOR Phase 3 Randomized Trial
abstract: Background: Severe asthma is often refractory to standard inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting bronchodilator therapies. Methods: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 1,061 patients aged 12 to 80 years with severe uncontrolled asthma received tezepelumab 210 mg subcutaneously or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER). Results: Tezepelumab reduced the annualized asthma exacerbation rate by 56% overall compared with placebo (AAER 0.93 vs 2.10; rate ratio 0.44; 95% CI, 0.37 to 0.53; p < 0.001). Exacerbation reductions were observed across baseline blood eosinophil counts (< 300 cells/uL and >= 300 cells/uL). Improvements were also seen in FEV1, symptom scores, and health-related quality of life. Adverse events were balanced across groups. Conclusions: Tezepelumab significantly reduced exacerbations and improved lung function in patients with severe uncontrolled asthma regardless of baseline eosinophil counts.

title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan versus Trastuzumab Emtansine for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer: The DESTINY-Breast03 Randomized Trial
abstract: Background: Antibody-drug conjugates have revolutionized treatment for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer. Methods: In the multicenter, open-label, Phase 3 DESTINY-Breast03 trial, 524 patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane were randomly assigned to receive trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) or trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1). Results: The 12-month progression-free survival was 75.8% with T-DXd versus 34.1% with T-DM1 (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.22 to 0.37; p < 0.001). Confirmed objective response occurred in 79.7% with T-DXd and 34.2% with T-DM1. Interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 10.5% of T-DXd patients (primarily grade 1 or 2). Conclusions: Trastuzumab deruxtecan demonstrated significant superior progression-free survival compared with trastuzumab emtansine in patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.

title: Upadacitinib as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis: Results from Phase 3 U-ACHIEVE and U-ACCOMPLISH Trials
abstract: Background: Selective Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibition represents a targeted oral approach for ulcerative colitis. Methods: Two randomized, double-blind Phase 3 induction trials and one maintenance trial enrolled 1,308 patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Patients received upadacitinib 45 mg once daily for 8 weeks (induction) followed by 15 mg or 30 mg once daily for 52 weeks (maintenance) versus placebo. Results: Clinical remission at week 8 was achieved by 26% and 34% of upadacitinib patients in the two induction trials compared with 5% and 4% in placebo groups (p < 0.001 for both). In the maintenance trial, 42% (15 mg) and 52% (30 mg) achieved clinical remission at week 52 versus 12% on placebo (p < 0.001). Rates of serious infections were low and consistent with JAK inhibitor profiles. Conclusions: Upadacitinib was significantly more effective than placebo as induction and maintenance therapy for patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
